name: Mui Ne
provinceNote: Mui Ne was in Binh Thuan, which merged into Lam Dong in 2025. It is still a beach town, not a Da Lat day trip.
dotReason: Worth it if you are already nearby
summary: Mui Ne is a beach strip northeast of the fishing town, known for kitesurfing, red dunes, and a white sand dune. It is a resort coast, spread along one road, and a long ride from Ho Chi Minh City.
fee: Beach is free; dunes charge small fees or jeep rides
getThere: About 4–5 hours by road from Ho Chi Minh City, or via Phan Thiet
seoTitle: Mui Ne travel guide — dunes, wind, and the ride from Ho Chi Minh City
seoDescription: How to get to Mui Ne, what the dunes are like, and which months suit the beach.
intro: The resort strip faces a long beach with a steady wind, which is why kitesurfers stay for a week and sightseers stay for two nights. The red dunes and the white dunes are outside the hotel row and are best at dawn or late afternoon.
Fairy Stream is a shallow walk inland. It is a small pleasure, not a national park.
gettingAround: Open-tour buses and private cars run from Ho Chi Minh City. Once there, the strip is a long road: rent a bicycle, use a taxi, or ride only if you are licensed. Walking between resorts is hotter and farther than the map suggests.

stayAreas.name: Resort strip
stayAreas.summary: Pick a hotel on the sand. Restaurants are attached or next door.

eat: Seafood and Russian-influenced visitor menus share the strip. For a local meal, ride toward the fishing harbor at Ham Tien or Phan Thiet.
interestsBody: Beach and dunes. Skip the dunes at noon. They are hot and the light is flat.
Resort living is the long Nguyen Dinh Chieu strip of wind, pools, and kitesurf schools.

interestCards.title: Resort Living
interestCards.summary: Pandanus and Asteria on the resort strip.

interestCards.title: Beaches
interestCards.summary: The resort-facing sand and the windy afternoon.

faqs.q: Is Mui Ne close to Da Lat?
faqs.a: No. They are in the same new province and several hours apart by road.
